R6E-duck-backcountry-0003.name: Unnamed wetland 670 m E of Clore River
R6E-duck-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: About 10 wetlands within 2 km (estimate): ducks move between them.
Beside Clore River: backwater or oxbow (estimate).
Elevation 833 m: under 900 m, open water later in fall.

flags.t: Route crosses protected area: Burnie River Protected Area. Hunting only where that park allows it, in open season. Check its bcparks.ca page (synopsis page 9, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: District 6. Within the 8 a day: 4 northern pintails, 4 canvasbacks, 2 Barrow's or common goldeneyes together, 2 harlequins. Possession 24: 12, 12, 6, 6.

plan: Drive: from District of Kitimat, about 93 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 54.17718, -127.72893, pull off on Cp 573 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 6.2 km W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 309 m, about 154 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 210 m NW of the spot at 825 m (54.15785, -127.81834). Water: unnamed wetland 100 m SW (estimate).
Hunt: ducks, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Set up on the shore with the wind at your back: ducks land into the wind (Tip). Shoot only birds you can retrieve.
Use: 12 gauge, steel 2 to 4 (non toxic shot only), modified or improved cylinder rated for steel, plugged to 3 shells (regs).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-9, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-16, closures 2026-10-16.
R6E-duck-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-9: about 10,278 hunter days a year for all big game (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.72 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
